newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: President Clinton signs nuclear test ban treaty.
newsitem.headline: President Clinton signs nuclear test ban treaty.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday signed the nuclear test ban treaty, designed to end atomic explosions in the atmosphere, underground or any other part of the environment.

"We are privileged today to witness a turning point in the history of efforts toward nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation," Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said as he opened the treaty for signature.

The foreign ministers of China, France, Russia and Britain, representing the other four known nuclear powers, signed immediately after Clinton. So did Japan's Ryutaro Hashimoto, prime minister of the only country scarred by Second World War nuclear attacks on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

But the treaty requires 44 nations with a nuclear potential to ratify it through their national legislatures before it goes into force. India, whose signature is necessary, has vowed never to sign "this unequal treaty, not now, not later" until the atomic powers devise a timetable for destroying their nuclear arsenals.

Nevertheless, most legal scholars believe that any state that signs the treaty is obligated to abide by it. At minimum the document is expected to create an international norm that would make testing a near moral impossibility.
